config.title: Design Notification System

intro.title: Design Notification System
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a notification system that displays alert messages on a web page, such as success or error updates. You will learn how to manage dynamic lists of notifications using React state and the useState hook. The core programming concepts involve handling arrays in state, conditionally rendering components, and using TypeScript for type safety. By the end, you will have a functional notification component that can add and remove alerts with user interactions.
intro.usecase: Notification systems are essential in modern web applications to keep users informed about important events. You'll find them in e-commerce platforms showing order confirmations, social media apps displaying new messages or likes, and productivity tools alerting about calendar events or task deadlines. As a developer, you'll implement these systems to provide timely feedback when users complete actions, receive updates, or encounter errors. This pattern appears in dashboard alerts, form submission confirmations, and real-time collaboration tools where immediate user awareness is critical.

objectives: Construct a Notification component with TypeScript interfaces for type safety
Initialize and manage notification state using React hooks
Implement a function to add new notifications to the system
Configure notification display logic with conditional rendering
Apply styling to differentiate notification types (success, error, warning)
Integrate a removal handler to clear notifications after display
Render a dynamic list of notifications with unique keys

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's start with the basics. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package using the import statement.

steps.title: Define Notification interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'Notification' with three properties: 'id' (string), 'message' (string), and 'type' (union type of 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error').
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Define the Notification interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a TypeScript interface that defines the shape of notification objects for the notification system.
successCriteria: The Notification interface is defined with id (string), message (string), and type ('info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error') properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined an interface, but check that all required properties (id, message, type) are present with the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Notification interface is not properly defined. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword and include all three properties with the specified types.

steps.title: Create NotificationSystem component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named NotificationSystem that returns a div element with the text 'Notification System' inside.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called NotificationSystem that returns JSX containing a div with the text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationSystem component is defined and returns a div with the text 'Notification System'.
successCriteria: A functional component named NotificationSystem exists and returns JSX with a div containing 'Notification System'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it's named exactly 'NotificationSystem' and returns the correct JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a function named NotificationSystem that returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize notifications state
steps.instruction: Inside your NotificationSystem component, initialize a state variable called 'notifications' using useState. Type it as Notification[] and set the initial value to an empty array.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to provide the generic type <Notification[]> to useState.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: typed state array
const [items, setItems] = useState<Item[]>([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a notifications state variable properly typed as an array of Notification objects, initialized as empty.
successCriteria: The notifications state is declared with useState, typed as Notification[], and initialized with an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've typed the state as Notification[] and initialized it with an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The notifications state isn't properly initialized. Check that you're using useState with the correct type and initial value.

steps.title: Create addNotification handler
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationSystem component, create a function called addNotification that takes a message (string) and type (Notification['type']) as parameters and adds a new notification object to the notifications array.
steps.hint: Use the setNotifications state setter to update the array. Create a new notification object with id, message, type, and timestamp properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The addNotification function is defined and ready to be used to add notifications to the state.
successCriteria: A function named addNotification exists that takes message and type parameters and updates the notifications state array with a new notification object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your addNotification function properly updates the notifications state using setNotifications and creates a complete notification object with all required properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addNotification function is not properly defined. Check that you've created a function with the correct name and parameters, and that it updates the notifications state correctly.

steps.title: Add container structure
steps.instruction: In the NotificationSystem component, return a div element with the class name 'notification-system' as the root JSX element.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a div that has a className attribute set to 'notification-system'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationSystem component now returns a div with the class 'notification-system', providing a structural container for the notification system.
successCriteria: The component returns a div element with className='notification-system'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a div element with the correct class name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div with className='notification-system' as the root element.

steps.title: Map and display notifications
steps.instruction: Inside the container div, map over the notifications state array to render each notification as a div element. For each notification, set a CSS class based on its type (e.g., 'info', 'success', 'error') and display its message inside the div.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the notifications array. Each notification should be rendered as a <div> with a className derived from its type property and containing its message property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The notifications array is rendered as a list of div elements inside the container, each with a className based on its type (e.g., 'notification-info') and displaying its message.
successCriteria: The map method is used on the notifications array to render each notification as a div with a className derived from its type property and containing its message property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started mapping the notifications, but make sure each div has a className based on the notification type and displays the message property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The notifications are not being displayed. Ensure you use the map method on the notifications array inside the container div to render each notification.

steps.title: Add close button to each notification
steps.instruction: Inside the map function, add a button element to each notification div that calls removeNotification with the notification's id when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a <button> inside the notification div with onClick={() => removeNotification(notification.id)} and appropriate text like 'Close'.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each notification should now have a close button that removes it when clicked.
successCriteria: Each notification div contains a button with onClick handler calling removeNotification with the correct id.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure each button has an onClick handler that calls removeNotification with the notification's id.
steps.feedbackWrong: The close buttons aren't properly implemented. Each notification needs a button that calls removeNotification with its id when clicked.

steps.title: Add controls to create notifications
steps.instruction: Add a div with the class 'controls' below the notification container, containing three buttons: one for 'info', one for 'success', and one for 'error'. Each button should have an onClick handler that calls addNotification with a sample message and the corresponding type.
steps.hint: Place the controls div after the notification-container div. Use inline arrow functions for onClick handlers, e.g., onClick={() => addNotification('Sample info message', 'info')}.
steps.analogousExample: // Adding control buttons
steps.expectedOutcome: Three buttons appear below the notifications, each labeled with its type ('info', 'success', 'error'). Clicking a button adds a new notification of that type with a sample message.
successCriteria: A div with class 'controls' is added after the notification-container div, containing three buttons with onClick handlers that call addNotification with appropriate sample messages and types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some controls, but make sure all three buttons are present with correct onClick handlers that call addNotification with the right type and a sample message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The controls are missing or incorrect. Ensure you add a div with class 'controls' containing three buttons, each with an onClick handler that calls addNotification with a sample message and the corresponding type.
